description: Plan step L4 (design step S3 minus the script executor; graph node schedules). The loop board's runtime core: run lock and beat, hand-over, inbox and emit, de-duplication, debounce and limits, the loop row's own events, the harness executor and run.ts for tell-main, harness and self entries, run records. script and check entries end as refused (unadopted / check-missing) because the executor and the approval path are blocked. Probe required. Depends on FEAT-010.
steps: Read loops design sec 4 (event table, keys per event), 6.1 (who runs: the project run lock, beat, handover.json), 6.3 (inbox, handleEvent, loop-duplicate, 7-day key memory, 'fourth in 24 hours'), 6.5 (harness actions and outcome conventions), 6.7 (debounce 5 s plugin / 30 s person, 30 and 6 per hour, merging, self-trigger window 10 minutes), 6.8 (missed runs and restart), 6.10 (records and outcomes), 10.1 (host contract table) and 16 S3. Read src/shared/pricing.ts nextPeakChange and tests/peak-mode.spec.ts; read reference/dsh-desktop-0.2.1-rc.3 for any host member this step uses (sessionController, agents) in the MAIN checkout.

Specs first (new tests/loops-inbox.spec.ts, tests/loops-run.spec.ts, tests/loops-watch.spec.ts; extend tests/fake-rc3.ts), see them fail: emit validates the event key structure and retries 3 times within 10 s; the same key within 7 days runs once and writes loop-duplicate, a fourth duplicate-ish event for the same entry in 24 h is flagged; debounce windows and per-hour limits, surplus events merge into the next run and are not lost; entries triggered by a command or action of the board itself are suppressed for 10 minutes; two child processes append to the inbox 200 times each with no lost or torn line; events left over from a stopped host are processed after start; run lock hand-over between two fake host processes sharing a user-level directory; loops.host-restarted fires once per process start with the start time in its key; loops.file-changed: fs.watch plus a 60 s size/mtime comparison, counts as one event after the file has been quiet for 60 s, deletion keys with 'gone'; loops.waiting-on-human: hourly read of the graph's open person-decided pendings and approval-waiting proposals (use the graph reading that exists on main: openItems-style data; do not require plain-ui), threshold in hours, quiet hours 22:00-08:00; channel.peak-changed derived from nextPeakChange with the key of the boundary instant, only when the pricing service exists; harness executor: calls the contributed run(action, event) with a 60 s limit, maps done/skipped/failed per sec 6.5, failed = row health degraded, done with a tell delivers (delivery itself is FEAT-012; here the tell goes through a deliver seam with a recording fake); script/check entries -> outcome refused with reason unadopted or check-missing, no message, page/health line written; records appended to runs.jsonl with outcome values delivered/ran/reported/delegated/skipped/suppressed/deferred/blocked/refused/unfinished and no output text.

Implement src/loops/lock.ts, inbox.ts, run.ts, harness.ts, file-watch.ts (the single function watchPaths(paths, onChange) both boards will use), records.ts, and the wiring in src/loops/index.ts: the service is provided inside ctx.inject(['sessionController']) as the design says; everything throws nowhere (activation and timers degrade to warn plus health). Do not add the script executor, runCommand, scriptDetail, commandText, checkCall calls or any child_process use (blocked cluster, impl-plan section 3); check with a test that src/loops/ imports no node:child_process.

Docs: ORCHESTRATION.md loop board section (runtime, outcomes), DESIGN.md interface/degradation tables. Probe: extend scenario loops so the row boots enabled with the new timers and exits clean. Commit at most twice. Messages carry gate results including the probe exit code.
acceptance_criteria: Every listed runtime case passes with injected clocks and fake hosts; the two-process inbox test shows no lost or torn line.
Entries with script or check actions never start a process and end refused with a reason shown to the person.
No timer, listener or tool handler can throw out of the row.
build, preflight, npm test and npm run probe exit 0 (or only the recorded baseline failures).
verification: npm test (TEMP = system temp directory) exits 0
findings:
Commit f9cd8f8 on rules-loops-impl (pushed to origin). Gates on the committed tree: npm run build 0, npm run preflight 0, npm test 0 (tests/rules-tickets.spec.ts did not show its intermittent timing failure this run, so it was not re-run), npm run probe 0 at 194/194 (193/193 before this step; one new check in scenario loops). Lint ratchets unchanged: eslint 250 suppressed, knip 21, jscpd 2 clones. Both the rules and the loops rows stay disabled: true in packages/hourness/cordis.patch.yml. docs/graph was deliberately not written: the step instruction forbade it, so the graph entry for this FEAT still has to be made by the caller.

An earlier interrupted run on this FEAT had already written all of src/loops/{lock,inbox,run,harness,file-watch,records,channel}.ts, the three new specs, the index.ts/registry.ts/service.ts/store.ts/guard wiring, the DESIGN.md and ORCHESTRATION.md sections and the probe check. That work was kept; what was finished in this pass: tests/loops-inbox.spec.ts never imported heldTimers from tests/loops-helpers.ts (8 of its 10 cases died with a ReferenceError and knip reported the helper as an unused export), 20 eslint errors across the three new specs (unnecessary type assertions, and one state.json cast that omitted run/at so the expected object was error-typed), the stale row comment in cordis.patch.yml ('no inbox, no runner, no storage, no tool or command yet') and the stale locale descriptions ('Registry and service only so far'), the section-18 heading marker, and the L3 verification line in 18.10 (still 193/193 and still naming only 18.7 and 18.8). No part of the pre-existing work was discarded: everything in it matched the frozen design 0.6, and the gate-FEAT-009 N4 deferral (rows 13 and 14 only with a pricing service) was closed by it.

Design gaps and deliberate narrowings, for the FEAT-012 and FEAT-013 steps:
1. Design 4.1's field table for loops.file-changed has size as a number, so there is no field that can say 'deleted'. A deletion is expressible only in the dedupe key (gone, with the mtime of the last version seen) and the payload carries size 0. Recorded in ORCHESTRATION.md 18.9; the design should either add a field or state that the key is the only carrier.
2. Design 6.1 names four ways a process starts running a project; only two exist here (a session of the project is created, or /loops is run in it). The DSH workspace registry listing and the main-agent holder record wait for FEAT-012 and FEAT-013.
3. ProjectDeps.holderHere has no reader yet (holder.ts lands with the delivery step), so src/loops/index.ts does not pass it: the whole hand-over mechanism is built and covered by specs but cannot fire on a production path, where holderHere is always 'not in this process'. FEAT-012 has to wire it, and only then does the lock really follow the main agent's session.
4. tell-main runs end held with reason holder-unreadable through the deliver seam (heldDeliver in run.ts, with DeliverRequest / DeliverResult defined there for FEAT-012). Design 6.4's holderState reasons other than holder-unreadable cannot be produced yet.
5. Design 6.7 does not say what happens to events waiting for an entry whose row withdraws its hand-over mid-wait. The implementation leaves the group pending, does not run it, and lets the events age out on the seven-day staleness rule.
6. channel.quota-low and channel.login-rejected (design 4.3, account level) need M6's quota reading and the machine-level runner; only channel.peak-changed is declared.
7. The 'fourth in 24 hours' of design 6.3 is read as: the fourth arrival of one dedupe key inside 24 hours degrades the row (two or three arrivals are an ordinary replay).
8. The dates in the ORCHESTRATION.md section-18 markers read 2026-11-02 while this machine's clock reads 2026-11-01; the new marker follows the sibling lines of the same section rather than the clock. Worth normalising once across section 18 if the clock is the authority.
